questions.stem: Quartzmarket spent $200 on a campaign that produced 10 new customers for its specialty coffee. What was the customer acquisition cost?
questions.explanation: Customer acquisition cost is total campaign spend divided by customers gained, so $200 divided by 10 gives $20 per customer. Dividing the other way would report customers per dollar instead.
questions.hint: Divide spend by the number of new customers.

questions.explanation: Customer acquisition cost is total campaign spend divided by customers gained, so $800 divided by 40 gives $20 per customer. Dividing the other way would report customers per dollar instead.
questions.hint: Divide spend by the number of new customers.

provenance.author: business-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles with fictional scenarios and data; no protected content used

questions.stem: A campaign by Quartzsummit cost $1,035 and won 45 new fitness apparel customers. What was the acquisition cost per customer?
questions.explanation: Spreading the $1,035 campaign cost across 45 new customers yields $23 per acquisition. Reversing the division would measure customers per dollar rather than cost per customer.
